minutes.headline: Selectmen filled the Council on Aging and Conservation Commission seats and began reworking how appointments are handled.
minutes.summary: The board heard public comment on volunteerism, then interviewed candidates and appointed one to the Council on Aging and four to the Conservation Commission. It corrected a Personnel Committee appointment, approved stop-sign traffic rule changes, and discussed giving the Personnel Committee a larger role in appointments. The town manager then reviewed first-quarter FY2015 financial results.

what_happened.line: The Select Board appointed one member to the Council on Aging vacancy, running through June 30, 2015.
The board appointed four members to the Conservation Commission, two to two-year terms and two to one-year terms.
The board rescinded a Personnel Committee appointment and named a different appointee through June 30, 2015; the earlier appointee will be directed to the Historical Commission.
The board approved a traffic rule change adding stop signs on Townsend Harbor Road at the Malpas Road intersection.
The board will send a draft appointment charge to the Personnel Committee, review the bylaw, and aim to adopt a new process by February or March.

why_it_matters: Who sits on town committees, and how they are chosen, is being reset, so residents who want to serve may face a different appointment process by spring 2015.

The first-quarter report points to meals tax collections and new growth running ahead of estimate, while tree removal after the July microburst overspent its line with no outside reimbursement expected; these bear on free cash and the tax levy.
watch_next: Personnel Committee feedback on the draft appointment charge, a possible workshop, and a bylaw review, with adoption aimed at February or March.
Whether the board appropriates the unbudgeted Chase Road solar net metering credits or uses them to backfill free cash.
